title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards covering API design, coding conventions, infrastructure, model-serving best practices, observability, performance targets, and a set of authoritative decision records (ADRs). It is intended as the canonical reference for engineers implementing new services and for reviewers during design and code reviews.

Scope

- Applies to all services and components owned by platforms and product teams that expose APIs, run model-serving workloads, or interact with the Redwood control/observability plane.
- Excludes ad-hoc scripts and experimental prototypes (those should follow the same principles but may be relaxed and explicitly labelled).

Principles

1. Predictability: APIs and services must behave consistently under expected load; defaults should favor stability.
2. Observability-first: Every service must emit metrics, traces, and structured logs sufficient to diagnose production issues.
3. Minimal blast radius: Defaults and infrastructure designs should minimize cross-service impact (rate limits, quotas, circuit breakers).
4. Reproducible infra: All infra must be defined in IaC with reviewed modules and automated CI.
5. Performance-aware: Model-serving and public APIs must meet documented SLOs; design for tail latency and cost efficiency.
api_standards:
- Naming & Versioning:
  - Use RESTful resource-based paths where appropriate (e.g., /v1/models/{id}/infer). For RPC-style operations (high-throughput internal services), use gRPC.
  - All public-facing APIs must include a semantic version in the path (v1, v2). Backwards-incompatible changes require a new major version.
  - Avoid verb-heavy resource names (prefer /jobs over /run-job).

- Request/Response design:
  - Use JSON for external APIs and protobufs for internal service-to-service contracts.
  - Responses must include a stable request_id and server_timestamps: {"request_id":"...","server_ts":"2026-03-04T12:00:00Z"} and an optional diagnostics field for debug_mode.
  - Implement pagination with standardized cursor-based tokens: {"next_cursor": "...", "items": [...]}.
error_handling_and_auth:
- Error handling:
  - Use structured error objects: {"code":"INVALID_INPUT","message":"...","details":{}}. Codes are uppercase, snake_case.
  - Map errors to HTTP status codes consistently (400 series for client, 500 for server). Include retryable flag.

- Rate limiting & quotas:
  - Default per-key rate limiting: 100 req/min for new API keys; contract-specific tiers override.
  - Services must return headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.

- Authentication & Authorization:
  - OAuth2 Bearer tokens for user-level flows; API keys for machine-to-machine. All tokens validated against central auth service (service-auth).
  - Role-based access checks performed at the service boundary.
coding_standards:
- Languages & toolchains:
  - Primary backend languages: Go (for infra & runtime), Python (data, evals, SDKs), and TypeScript (frontend, control plane).
  - Use the company-approved linters and formatters: gofmt/goimports, golangci-lint, black + isort (Python), ESLint + Prettier (TS).

- Testing
  - Unit tests: target >= 90% coverage for core libraries; >= 70% for service handlers.
  - Integration tests: required for APIs that interact with model-serving or billing. Use CI stages: unit -> integration -> e2e (staged infra).
  - Contract tests: any change to protobufs or public JSON contracts must include contract tests and a compatibility check job in CI.

- Code review & ownership:
  - Every PR must have at least one reviewer from the owning team and a secondary reviewer for cross-cutting changes (security, infra, runtime).
  - Tag reviewers using team shortcuts. Large changes must include a design doc link.
infrastructure_standards:
- IaC:
  - All cloud resources defined in Terraform modules maintained in infra-modules repo. Changes require a pull request and automated plan/apply pipeline.
  - Modules must have documented interfaces, inputs, outputs, and examples.

- Networking & tenancy:
  - Services must be designed for multi-tenant routing (namespace isolation). VPCs and subnetting follow the standard network map in infra-modules/network.
  - Private deployments (customer VPC/on-prem) must expose a standardized ingress and egress pattern; see onprem-packaging guidelines.

- Secrets & keys:
  - All secrets stored in KMS-backed secret store (HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS+Secret Manager). No plaintext secrets in repos or logs.
model_serving_standards:
- Packaging & model artifacts:
  - Models must be packaged with a manifest (manifest.yaml) declaring architecture, tokenizer, expected precision (fp16/int8), quantization profile id, KV cache support, and evaluation artifacts (eval id / baseline). Example manifest:

    ```yaml
    id: redwood-llama-13b-q4f16
    arch: transformer
    framework: torch
    quantization: q4f16
    tokenizer: tiktoken-v1
    supports_kv_cache: true
    baseline_eval: evals/2026-01-23/conv-quality-v1
    ```

- Runtime requirements:
  - Kernels must support batched inference. The serving runtime should expose configurable batching windows (max_wait_ms, max_batch_size). Default: max_wait_ms=5, max_batch_size=32 for hosted low-latency endpoints.
  - KV / prefix caching enabled for chat-style workloads. Cache TTLs should be workload-specific and documented in the model manifest.

- Quantization & precision:
  - Quantization profiles are centrally curated (see quantization-profiles). Each profile must specify expected throughput uplift and estimated quality delta. Quantization is allowed for production only after A/B evaluation shows <= 1% quality regression on guarded prompts.

- Rollouts & Canaries:
  - Use gradual rollout: 0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated quality gates (baseline regression checks) at each step. Canary window default = 2 hours and minimum 1000 inference requests.
observability_standards:
- Metrics:
  - Emit Prometheus-style metrics with the following required counters/gauges for every service:
    - requests_total{route,method,result}
    - request_latency_seconds_bucket{route}
    - tokens_generated_total{model,route}
    - gpu_utilization_percent{instance}
    - cache_hit_ratio{model}

  - Metric naming: snake_case, dot-free, include key tags (model, route, region).

- Tracing:
  - Use OpenTelemetry. Span naming: service.operation (e.g., infer.generate_request). All root spans must include request_id and model_id attributes.

- Structured logging:
  - JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, request_id, caller, message, details (optional). Avoid PII in logs.

- Dashboards & Alerts:
  - Standard dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), error budget burn rate, tokens per second, GPU pool utilization, cache hit ratio.
  - Alerting thresholds (examples):
    - High tail latency: p99 > 500ms for hosted gen endpoints -> P1 alert.
    - Error rate spike: error_rate_5m > 1% absolute increase -> P1.
    - GPU OOM rate > 0.5% over 10m -> P2.
  - Alert runbooks must link to oncall/incident-response runbooks.
performance_slos_and_testing:
- Service-level SLOs (example defaults):
  - Hosted inference API (text generation): Availability: 99.9% monthly; Latency: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (<128 tokens); p99 < 800ms.
  - Embeddings API: Availability: 99.95%; p95 < 150ms.
  - Dedicated/GPU-backed internal batches: throughput targets documented per GPU type in gpu-fleet-and-capacity.

- Load testing:
  - All public endpoints undergo load testing before launch with a baseline scenario and two stress scenarios (100% expected peak, 3x expected peak). Use the benchmarking-and-perf-suite to generate realistic traffic (token distributions, sequence length).

- Cost-awareness:
  - Services must include token-level cost metrics and expose cost-per-request to the Console for chargeback and optimizations. Cost budgets and alerts for dedicated pools are required.
adrs:
- ADR-2025-09: Runtime language choice
  - Status: Accepted (2025-09-18)
  - Context: Evaluate runtime language for high-throughput inference engine.
  - Decision: Implement core runtime in Go + C++ kernels. Provide Python bindings for tooling and ops.
  - Consequences: Faster GC and lower tail latency for control plane. Requires cross-language CI and native extension packaging.
  - Owner: Runtime team (lead: Ethan Kim)

- ADR-2025-11: Quantization profile governance
  - Status: Accepted (2025-11-02)
  - Context: Allow quantized models in production while minimizing quality regressions.
  - Decision: Centralized quantization profile registry and mandatory A/B regression checks (<=1% quality delta on guarded prompts).
  - Consequences: Slower onboarding for new quant profiles but safer rollouts.
  - Owner: Applied ML & Evals (lead: Rosa Martinez)

- ADR-2026-01: API versioning strategy
  - Status: Accepted (2026-01-12)
  - Context: Multiple breaking changes needed across model infer schema as we add function-calling and structured outputs.
  - Decision: Use path-based major versions (e.g., /v1/, /v2/) and maintain compatibility policy for 12 months per major version. Deprecation notices published 90 days before EOL.
  - Consequences: Extra maintenance for multi-version support; clearer upgrade path for customers.
  - Owner: API Standards WG (lead: Michael Chen)
operational_procedures:
1. Service Onboarding Checklist (must be completed before Prod):
   - Design doc reviewed in Architecture channel.
   - IaC modules created and reviewed.
   - Metrics/traces/logs instrumented and dashboards created.
   - Load test executed with reports attached.
   - Security review completed.

2. Model Rollout Procedure:
   - Register model manifest in model-catalog.
   - Run offline evals and store results in eval-harness.
   - Canary rollout with automated regression checks; hold if quality delta > threshold.
ownership_and_maintenance:
- This document is owned by the Architecture & Standards working group (contact: architecture@redwood.internal). Standards should be reviewed quarterly and updated when ADRs are accepted or infrastructure changes (e.g., new GPU types).

Appendix: Example CI job snippets

- Terraform plan CI step (example):
  - name: terraform-plan
    run: |
      terraform init -backend-config="bucket=tf-state-${{ github.ref }}"
      terraform plan -out=plan.tfout

- Contract compatibility check (example):
  - name: protobuf-compatibility
    run: |
      buf build && buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'

If there are questions or proposed changes, please open a PR against this page or raise them in the #architecture-standards Slack channel.
